strengths: The combination of adversarially generated training distributions, bootstrapped targets, and learned Sinkhorn initializations is a useful contribution. It addresses amortized OT computation without requiring training examples from the eventual application dataset.

The Hilbert projective loss appropriately handles the scaling ambiguity of Sinkhorn potentials. Proposition 4.3 provides a sound residual-to-solution error bound under the positive-kernel assumptions, giving a principled justification for using partially refined predictions as targets.

The reported improvements are substantial across four image datasets. For example, Table 2 reduces the mean iterations required for 0.01 marginal constraint violation on CIFAR from 47 with standard initialization and 17 with Gaussian initialization to 3. Five independent training runs, 500 evaluation pairs per dataset, and the generator-versus-noise ablation strengthen this evidence.

The algorithms and appendix provide useful architecture, hyperparameter, training-budget, and hardware details, together with a code link. Retaining ordinary Sinkhorn refinement makes the learned initialization practically usable beyond its initial prediction accuracy.
weaknesses: The central universality claim exceeds the evidence. Theorem 4.1 requires matching input/output dimensions and a Lipschitz constraint, whereas the implemented generator uses a 392-dimensional latent space for pairs of 784-dimensional distributions and does not enforce that constraint. The authors acknowledge these departures, but still use the theorem to dismiss generator coverage as a bottleneck. Even full support would not establish uniform prediction accuracy or convergence of the adversarial training procedure. Four image datasets demonstrate useful transfer, but do not establish accurate approximation for arbitrary distribution pairs; concentrated, sparse, and non-image histograms would provide more direct tests.

The closest learned baseline, Amos et al. (2022), is explicitly excluded based on an asserted failure under distribution shift, without comparative results supporting that assertion. Training its dual-objective approach on the same generated samples would help distinguish the contributions of data generation and bootstrapping. The random-noise ablation is useful but insufficient to establish an advantage over existing amortized OT learning. The claim of being the first meta neural OT solver also needs qualification given this acknowledged prior work.

The accuracy metric is inconsistently defined. Algorithm 1 returns the transport component <C, Gamma>, while Section 5.2 defines the reference value as the minimum of <C, Gamma> - epsilon H(Gamma) from Problem 3.3. These quantities differ even after convergence, so the statement that the algorithm's returned distance converges to that minimum is incorrect. The manuscript must clarify which functional is used throughout the relative-error experiments and specify how reference solutions are computed. This directly affects interpretation of the few-percent accuracy and standalone-solver claims, although the marginal-violation results remain informative.

The generator theorem contains additional, repairable mathematical problems. ReLU is noninvertible and produces singular probability mass on the orthant boundary, so the stated density formula involving q^{-1} cannot hold there as written; Appendix A cannot simply discard ReLU without qualification. Remark 4.2 is also false in its stated generality: q(z) = ReLU(z/2 + 1) satisfies the assumptions, but q(q(z)) is always at least 1 and therefore lacks support on (0,1). An interior, almost-everywhere density statement and a separate support argument would be more appropriate.

The practical efficiency evidence remains limited. Figure 8 compares wall-clock performance only against standard initialization, omitting the stronger Gaussian baseline, and gives insufficient detail about timing methodology. All experiments use one resolution, cost, regularization value, and batch size. Matched-accuracy timings against Gaussian initialization, scaling measurements, and an amortization analysis for the reported 40-minute training cost are needed to establish the practical advantage beyond the demonstrated configuration.
